title: Retain sources and read Annals delivery activity
summary: Preserve unchanged source bytes, retrieve retained works, and read delivery metadata with explicit lifecycle and timestamp meaning.
use_when: Immutable source bytes should enter the Annals library while interpretation is intentionally deferred.
A retained work must be listed or inspected by its work label.
Retained source text or recent source-delivery activity must be read without model interpretation.
do_not_use_when: The source should be reconciled with the evidence-backed idea map now.
The requested operation is application workflow, summarization, or inferred structured fields rather than exact source retention.
The material is not nonblank UTF-8 source text.
outcome: One content-addressed immutable work is retained or recognized, with a completed manual source delivery and no corpus revision change.
effects: Reads a UTF-8 file or standard input and records a source delivery.
Retains previously unseen exact bytes under one normalized-unique work label, or selects the existing work when the bytes are already present.
Does not invoke a model and does not change concepts, evidence, commits, or HEAD.
authority: The Annals library owns retained work bytes, content identity, work labels, and delivery history.
Source filesystem timestamps are captured metadata, not authorship, publication, or document-content dates.
success: `annals work add` reports the retained or recognized canonical work label.
`annals work show <LABEL>` returns the complete unchanged text and first-retained metadata.
failure_and_recovery: An existing label attached to different bytes is a conflict and no replacement occurs.
When exact bytes already exist, use the canonical retained work rather than assuming the requested alternate label was created.
Use a registered named library or explicit operator config/path; Annals never falls back to `./annals.db`.

Invalid source or label conflict leaves retained bytes unchanged. Interrupted source-bearing manual commands are finalized by the next command with manual_ingestion_interrupted. Choose first-seen or completed to inspect failures without ingestion time.
privacy: The complete unchanged source is retained in the selected local Annals library.
No source content is sent to Nucleus or a model by this capability.
does_not_authorize: Application of any pending corpus change.
Deletion or replacement of retained source bytes.

consumers.statement: General libraries can retain supplied wants, preferences, career accounts, notes, and other nonblank UTF-8 source documents. This preserves wording without creating application workflow or inferred fields.
A local user or agent that needs to preserve one immutable source while deliberately deferring interpretation may use this capability.
This is not a note, summary, action-backlog or model-assisted interpretation surface.

preconditions.statement: The caller selects a configured readable Annals library with the immutable general role. Retention requires a writable library and nonblank UTF-8 bytes. Standard input requires an explicit label.
A requested work label must not already identify different retained bytes.

inputs.statement: Input is one UTF-8 file or standard-input stream, an optional explicit work label for files, and the normal Annals library/configuration selectors.
Binary, blank, multi-work, reconciliation, replacement, deletion, and model instructions are not accepted by this capability.
Activity accepts UTC half-open since/until windows, one timestamp basis, and status/channel filters. Positive relative durations use s,m,h,d,w; RFC3339 or UTC date input is accepted.

outputs.statement: Retention returns its durable work/delivery receipt. Work list returns a schema-two items/has_more page with a default limit of 20. Increase positive --limit to read more. Work show returns the selected work's complete content and structure.

lately returns delivery metadata, lifecycle/retention/missing-time counts, resolved UTC window and filters, without source text, headings, quotations, document-internal dates, raw runner diagnostics, row IDs, or dedicated source-path fields.

data_semantics.statement: Content identity and duplicate recognition are local to the selected library. Separate libraries have separate retained sources and corpus history.
Retention stores previously unseen exact bytes or recognizes an existing byte-identical work; recognition does not create the requested alternate label.
A completed manual source delivery records the occasion of supply, while the work is the immutable content object and the corpus remains unchanged.

Each delivery has independent processing/completed/failed lifecycle, new/duplicate retention disposition, and retained/pending/applied/recorded result. Only applied names a corpus revision. Retention and work-add completion are atomic; input-integration applied result and corpus revision are atomic.

first_retained_at belongs to exact retained work bytes. first_seen_at, ingested_at, and completed_at belong to one delivery. Captured filesystem times are metadata, not authorship, publication, source events, or continued path watching.

identity_and_units.statement: Exact SHA-256 content identity selects one immutable work, and its normalized-unique work label is the supported public selector.
Captured source filesystem times are metadata timestamps, not authorship, publication, or document-content dates.
Retention publishes no usage, price, or accounting measurement.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Work show returns the complete unchanged retained UTF-8 text and first-retained metadata for the selected work.
A successful command reports the library result committed by that invocation; no cached catalog or remote copy is served.

Activity basis governs membership and newest-first ordering. Missing basis timestamps omit matching deliveries and contribute to missing_time_count. --until defaults to report start and --since to seven days before resolved end.

access.statement: A registered name scopes ordinary commands as annals library NAME COMMAND. The catalog resolves and verifies stable library identity and managed paths; unknown names fail without creation. Operator config/path selection remains supported.
The supported boundary is the local Annals CLI and an explicitly resolved library selected by command line, environment, or configuration.
No network, remote sharing, direct SQLite write, or implicit current-directory database surface is provided.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One successful supply records one manual source delivery and either creates one immutable work or selects the existing byte-identical work without advancing corpus HEAD.
A label conflict fails without replacing either retained work, and retained bytes have no update-in-place lifecycle.

Invalid source or label conflict leaves retained bytes unchanged. Interrupted source-bearing manual commands are finalized by the next command with manual_ingestion_interrupted. Choose first-seen or completed to inspect failures without ingestion time.

operational_limits.statement: One invocation accepts one nonblank UTF-8 source; standard input requires an explicit label.
No maximum accepted source size, retention capacity, throughput, or wall-clock latency is promised by this contract.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 3 identifies these retention semantics independently of the Annals provider release and library schema.
No cross-release client compatibility window or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Retention invokes no model, Nucleus, network, or other product and has no substantive cross-system reliance.
